markscheme.html:
Correct answer: A

A: Correct: clamping at the centre enforces zero displacement at the midpoint (node) and the free ends correspond to antinodes in the standing-wave model; only symmetric modes satisfy both ends simultaneously. The resonant frequencies are not exact integer harmonics for a real clamped-free beam, so describing them as “only odd harmonics” is not strictly correct.

B: Incorrect as stated: while a simple node–antinode string/air-column model would suggest an odd-multiple pattern, a real rod/beam does not have resonant frequencies that are exact odd integer multiples, so “only odd harmonics” is misleading here.

C: Incorrect: the central clamp imposes a node at the midpoint, so not all mode symmetries are permitted; modes must satisfy the midpoint node and free-end conditions.

D: Incorrect: multiple resonant modes are possible (a set of allowed symmetric modes), not just a single mode.

question.html:
A metal rod is clamped at the middle and free at both ends. Which statement best describes the resonance modes possible for this configuration?

  1. Only modes that are symmetric about the clamp (with a node at the clamp and antinodes at the free ends)
  2. Only odd harmonics of the fundamental
  3. All integer harmonics of the fundamental
  4. Only one unique mode is possible
